equation_request.abstract: We investigate the subclass of reversible functions that are self-inverse and relate them to reversible circuits that are equal to their reverse circuit, which are called palindromic circuits. We precisely determine which self-inverse functions can be realized as a palindromic circuit. For those functions that cannot be realized as a palidromic circuit, we find alternative palindromic representations that require an extra circuit line or quantum gates in their construction. Our analyses make use of involutions in the symmetric group $S_{2^{n}}$ which are isomorphic to self-inverse reversible function on $n$ variables.

specification.problem: Characterize which self-inverse reversible functions f on n bits (involutions in S_{2^n}) can be realized by a palindromic reversible circuit, i.e., a gate sequence equal to its own reverse, and give a tiny explicit palindromic realization.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Finite scope chosen here (no experiment_scope supplied): n-line reversible circuits over the library of NOT, CNOT and multiple-controlled Toffoli gates (all involutive), the formal definition of palindromic circuits, the structural consequence f = C g C^{-1}, a candidate cycle-type criterion derived from it, and one explicit instance on n=3 lines (the transposition swapping |000> and |111>, realized by a 9-gate palindrome). Outside scope: the paper's exact statement/proof of the realizability theorem, the constructions using an extra circuit line, and the constructions using quantum (non-permutation) gates for non-realizable involutions; the abstract gives no details of these.

symbols.meaning: number of circuit lines / Boolean variables
basis state of the n lines, encoded as integer \sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i 2^{i-1} (line 1 is the least significant bit)
reversible function, a bijection on \{0,1\}^n, identified with a permutation in S_{2^n}
symmetric group on the 2^n basis states
reversible circuit as an ordered gate list, g_1 applied first
symbols.domain: finite sequence of gates from the library

symbols.meaning: Toffoli gate with c control lines (c=0 is NOT, c=1 is CNOT) and one target line
number of disjoint transpositions (2-cycles) in the cycle decomposition of the involution f
conjugating permutation realized by the first half of an odd-length palindrome

equations.label: Self-inverse reversible functions are involutions of S_{2^n}
equations.latex: f \in S_{2^n},\quad f \circ f = \mathrm{id} \iff f = f^{-1} \iff f^2 = e
equations.description: A reversible function on n variables is a permutation of the 2^n basis states; it is self-inverse exactly when it is an involution (including the identity).
equations.abstract_quote: involutions in the symmetric group $S_{2^{n}}$ which are isomorphic to self-inverse reversible function on $n$ variables
equations.justification: Direct restatement of the abstract's identification of self-inverse functions with involutions.
assumptions: Basis states encoded as integers via x \mapsto \sum_i x_i 2^{i-1}.

equations.label: Circuit function, reverse circuit, and palindromic condition
equations.latex: f_G = g_k \circ \cdots \circ g_1,\qquad f_{G^R} = g_1 \circ \cdots \circ g_k = f_G^{-1}\ (\text{if } g_i^2=e),\qquad G \text{ palindromic} \iff g_i = g_{k+1-i}\ \forall i
equations.description: The circuit computes the composition of its gates; with involutive gates the reverse circuit computes the inverse function; a palindromic circuit is one identical to its reverse, hence realizes a self-inverse function.
equations.abstract_quote: reversible circuits that are equal to their reverse circuit, which are called palindromic circuits
equations.justification: Formalization of 'equal to their reverse circuit'; the inverse property uses the standard fact that NOT/CNOT/Toffoli gates are involutions.
assumptions: Gate library consists of involutive gates (NOT, CNOT, multiple-controlled Toffoli).

equations.label: Structure of palindromic circuits
equations.latex: k=2m+1:\ f_G = C \circ g_{m+1} \circ C^{-1},\ C = g_m \circ \cdots \circ g_1;\qquad k=2m:\ f_G = \mathrm{id}
equations.description: An odd-length palindrome realizes a conjugate of its single middle gate; an even-length palindrome over involutive gates realizes the identity.
equations.justification: Follows algebraically from eq_2: the second half of the palindrome is the inverse of the first half when all gates are involutions.
assumptions: Involutive gate library as in eq_2.

equations.label: Cycle type of a Toffoli gate
equations.latex: T_c \text{ on } n \text{ lines} = \prod_{j=1}^{2^{\,n-1-c}} (a_j\ b_j),\quad\text{so } t(T_c) = 2^{\,n-1-c},\ 0 \le c \le n-1
equations.description: A Toffoli gate with c controls flips the target on exactly 2^{n-1-c} input pairs that differ only in the target bit; it is a product of that many disjoint transpositions. Conjugation by C preserves cycle type.
equations.justification: Standard counting of inputs satisfying the control condition; conjugacy classes of S_N are determined by cycle type.
assumptions: Controls may be positive or negative; this does not change the cycle type.

equations.label: Candidate realizability criterion (derived, not taken from the paper)
equations.latex: f \text{ realizable as palindromic circuit} \iff t(f) \in \{0\} \cup \{2^{j} : 0 \le j \le n-1\}
equations.description: Combining eq_3 and eq_4: palindromic circuits over Toffoli gates realize exactly the identity and the conjugates of single Toffoli gates, i.e., involutions whose number of transpositions is a power of two not exceeding 2^{n-1}. Sufficiency uses that NOT/CNOT/Toffoli generate all of S_{2^n}, so any f of matching cycle type is some conjugate C T_c C^{-1}.
equations.justification: This is the criterion implied by eq_3-eq_4 under the involutive-Toffoli gate library; the abstract only says the class is 'precisely determined' and the paper's actual statement is not available here.
assumptions: Gate library is exactly NOT/CNOT/multiple-controlled Toffoli (no ancilla, no quantum gates).
Generation of S_{2^n} by this library for n \ge 3 (and S_4 for n=2) is used for sufficiency.

equations.label: Tiny instance: n=3, f=(000\ 111) as a 9-gate palindrome
equations.description: The Toffoli T_{1,2->3} swaps 110 and 111; C maps 110->000 and 111->111, so C T C^{-1} swaps 000 and 111 and fixes all other states. The gate list is its own reverse. By contrast, an involution such as (001\ 010)(011\ 100)(101\ 110) with t(f)=3 violates eq_5 and would need the paper's extra-line or quantum constructions.
equations.justification: Explicit small example constructed from eq_3; checked by hand on the inputs 000, 111 and 001 under the stated bit encoding.
assumptions: Bit string written as x_1x_2x_3 with line 1 leftmost in the string; gates applied left to right.

registers.name: lines
registers.role: the n reversible circuit lines carrying the input x and, after the circuit, f(x)

specification.initial_state: Computational basis state |x_1 x_2 ... x_n> for the input x to be mapped; no ancilla lines in the chosen scope.

steps.description: Given an involution f (eq_1), compute its cycle decomposition and the number of transpositions t(f).
Decide realizability with the cycle-type criterion: t(f) must be 0 or a power of two 2^j with j <= n-1 (derived criterion, see assumptions).
If realizable with t(f)=2^{n-1-c}, pick a Toffoli gate T_c with the same cycle type and find a permutation C with f = C T_c C^{-1}; synthesize C as a Toffoli-gate circuit (g_1,...,g_m).
Output the palindrome G = (g_1,...,g_m, T_c, g_m,...,g_1), which satisfies g_i = g_{k+1-i} and computes f.
Instance n=3: f=(000 111) realized by the explicit 9-gate palindrome.

specification.classical_postprocessing: Verification only: apply the circuit to each of the 2^n basis inputs (classical simulation of permutation gates) and check that the resulting truth table equals f and that the gate list equals its reverse.
assumptions: No experiment_scope was supplied; the smallest useful construction (odd-length palindrome as conjugate of one Toffoli gate) and the instance n=3, f=(000 111) were chosen by the reconstruction.
Gate library restricted to NOT, CNOT and multiple-controlled Toffoli gates, all of which are involutions.
The realizability criterion eq_5 is derived from group-theoretic reasoning, not read from the paper; the paper's precise theorem may be stated differently or use a different gate library.
Integer encoding x = sum_i x_i 2^{i-1}; gate sequences are applied left to right.
missing_information: The paper's exact statement and proof of which self-inverse functions admit palindromic circuits.
The construction with one extra circuit line for non-realizable involutions (how the function is embedded and which palindromic form is used).
The construction using quantum gates (e.g., which non-permutation gates, such as controlled roots of NOT, are allowed and how palindromicity is defined for them).
Whether negative controls, mixed-polarity gates, or other gate libraries are permitted in the paper's definition.
